This indicates the decision was driven predominantly by visual opacities and patterns detected in the X-ray rather than patient demographics or symptoms.

#### Plain-Language Clinician Summary
The artificial intelligence diagnostic system evaluated the patient's chest X-ray alongside clinical indicators (age 61, female, cough present, no fever) and classified the case as **TUBERCULOSIS** with high confidence (97.6%). 

The adaptive fusion network heavily prioritized the visual patterns present in the chest X-ray (importance weight ~99%) over the clinical variables. Clinicians should review the saved GradCAM heatmap (`outputs\gradcam_result.png`) to inspect the specific regions of the lung fields that drove this high-confidence prediction and correlate these findings with sputum smear/culture results or confirmatory molecular testing (e.g., GeneXpert).
